I’ve got about 9 mu of flat, irrigable land here in Quzhou, and I’ve been farming it for more than twenty years. Around here, nearly everyone does the wheat-maize double crop — it’s the safest way to make sure we have grain to sell and straw for the animals. My winter wheat went in last October with an improved variety, same as my neighbors use. Right now it’s April and the wheat is greening up, so I’ve already given it the winter irrigation and I’m getting ready for the greening and jointing water. I don’t mess around with fertilizer — the extension fellow said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but my cousin tried cutting back two years ago and his wheat turned yellow at jointing, so I’m sticking with about 18 kg N per mu for the wheat and a bit less for the maize. I use compound fertilizer for phosphorus and potassium too, because the soil here needs it. For the summer maize, I’ll sow hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June. There’s only about five or six days between harvest and planting, so I use no-tillage direct seeding — learned that from the machine operator who works our village. I irrigate the maize twice if the summer rains are weak, and I spray pesticides a few times on both crops to keep weeds, aphids, and corn borers under control. I expect around 520 kg per mu of wheat and 600 kg per mu of maize if the weather holds. It’s not fancy, but it puts food on the table and pays the bills.

I irrigate wheat four times and maize twice because groundwater pumping is expensive but necessary in this semi-arid climate.
